quote: However, in the four magnetic field alignments with RF present (RF on → RF on), the same animals showed consistent alignment relative to the magnetic field (mean direction: 196°, p < 0.01, R* = 1.307, n = 18, …).
note: Name: printed and accepted both Chelydra serpentina (Linnaeus, 1758); Reptile Database page. Licence: PLOS ONE article; CC BY 4.0 per Crossref and the PMC page (audit 246). The abstract reports that the other two sequences (RF off then on, RF on then off) were disoriented. The authors read the RF effect as a change in the pattern of magnetic input rather than its removal; this is a statement about the response, not a measured threshold. 'The same animals' in the quote are the turtles first exposed with RF present, not those of the RF off → RF off record; six turtles were tested per day and n is 18 per initial-exposure group.
